$comment: Camera preset library. Shared by the editor and the fixture builder. Presets are a convenience only: every intrinsic is copied inline into the plan when a camera is placed, so a plan opened without this file is still fully specified. intrinsicsSource records how much to trust the numbers -- see CONVENTIONS.md section 4. Presets that share a 'body' are the lenses of one camera: the palette lists the body once and places the entry marked 'bodyDefault', and the inspector offers the others under Lens.

presets.label: FLIR T650sc — 25° lens
presets.$note: 640x480 microbolometer at 17 um pitch gives the sensor size; the 24.6 mm standard lens gives 24.9° x 18.8°.

presets.label: FLIR A700 — 80° lens
presets.$note: The A700 body (7.68 x 5.76 mm, see the 24 deg lens) with lens T300805, printed as 5 mm and 80 x 63 deg (rev. 93944). Under a pinhole 5 mm gives 75.05 x 59.88 deg, narrower than printed; 80 deg would need 4.58 mm. The printed focal length is kept. The sources do not say whether rounding or distortion accounts for the difference, so calibrate before reconstructing. See docs/datasheets/README.md.

presets.label: FLIR A700 — 42° lens
presets.$note: The A700 body (7.68 x 5.76 mm, see the 24 deg lens) with lens T300239, printed as 10 mm and 42 x 32 deg. Under a pinhole 10 mm gives 42.01 x 32.13 deg, which agrees with the printed angles. See docs/datasheets/README.md.

presets.label: FLIR A700 — 24° lens
presets.$note: The A700 24 deg f/1.0 Professional Science Kit sheet (P/N 85903-0102, rev. 98866) prints 640 x 480 at 12 um pitch, which gives the 7.68 x 5.76 mm sensor, and this lens as 18 mm. Derived from those: 24.1 x 18.2 deg and 0.67 mrad/px, against the 24 x 18 deg designation. FLIR also lists a 17 mm f/1.3 lens as 24 deg (25.5 x 19.2 deg here); if that is the lens fitted, type 17 mm. The body's 6, 14, 42 and 80 deg lenses are under Lens. See docs/datasheets/README.md.

presets.label: FLIR A700 — 14° lens
presets.$note: The A700 body (7.68 x 5.76 mm, see the 24 deg lens) with lens T300241, printed as 29 mm and 14 x 10 deg (rev. 79639). Under a pinhole 29 mm gives 15.09 x 11.34 deg, wider than printed; 14 deg would need 31.3 mm. The printed focal length is kept; calibrate before reconstructing. See docs/datasheets/README.md.

presets.label: FLIR A700 — 6° lens
presets.$note: The A700 body (7.68 x 5.76 mm, see the 24 deg lens) with lens T300095, printed as 70 mm and 6 x 4.5 deg (rev. 79192, which also allows distortion below 4.2%). Under a pinhole 70 mm gives 6.28 x 4.71 deg, wider than printed; 6 deg would need 73.3 mm. The printed focal length is kept; calibrate before reconstructing. See docs/datasheets/README.md.

presets.label: FLIR A8303sc — 17 mm lens
presets.$note: The A8303sc body with its 17 mm lens: 55.6 deg x 33.0 deg, 0.82 mrad per pixel, derived from the 14 um array -- the sheet prints the lens by focal length and no field of view.

presets.label: FLIR A8303sc — 25 mm lens
presets.$note: Cooled InSb, 1280x720 at 14 um pitch, f/4.0, 60 Hz at full window, all printed on the A8300sc sheet. The 25 mm lens gives 39.4 deg x 22.8 deg, 0.56 mrad per pixel, derived from the array -- the sheet prints no field of view. It lists four lenses, 17, 25, 50 and 100 mm, and each is a preset of this body; the inspector's Lens field switches between them. Digital zoom is 1x/2x on this camera; set it in the Zoom field rather than by editing the focal length.

presets.label: FLIR A8303sc — 50 mm lens
presets.$note: The A8303sc body with its 50 mm lens: 20.3 deg x 11.5 deg, 0.28 mrad per pixel, derived from the 14 um array -- half the 25 mm lens's field at twice its detail.

presets.label: FLIR A8303sc — 100 mm lens
presets.$note: The A8303sc body with its 100 mm lens: 10.2 deg x 5.8 deg, 0.14 mrad per pixel, derived from the 14 um array -- a quarter of the 25 mm lens's field at four times its detail.

presets.label: FLIR K65
presets.$note: The K65 sheet in FLIR's 2018 Fire Products catalog (P/N 72202-0303, rev. 46856) prints 320 x 240 at 25 um pitch, which gives the 8 x 6 mm sensor, a 9 mm lens, 8-14 um and 60 Hz. Under a pinhole 9 mm gives 47.9 x 36.9 deg, not the printed 51 x 38 deg, and no one focal length reproduces both angles. The current product page lists 7.5-13 um instead. The recorded video is not radiometric; its 2x digital zoom goes in the Zoom field. See docs/datasheets/README.md.

presets.label: FLIR ONE Pro
presets.$note: The thermal camera of the 2017 FLIR ONE Pro (sheet 17-1746-OEM-FLIROne_Pro, 2017-06-06): 160 x 120 at 12 um pitch gives 1.92 x 1.44 mm. The sheet prints no focal length; 1.92 / (2 tan 27.5 deg) = 1.84414 mm reproduces its 55 deg horizontal field and gives 42.7 deg vertical, inside the printed 43 +/- 1 deg. The app's 1440 x 1080 video is processed from this 160 x 120 array. The current product page lists 50 x 43 deg, which this sheet contradicts. See docs/datasheets/README.md.

presets.label: GoPro HERO — wide, 1080p
presets.$note: Approximates the ~122° wide mode as an ideal pinhole. The real lens is strongly non-rectilinear, so this is adequate for framing checks and NOT adequate for reconstruction — calibrate and populate `distortion` first.

presets.label: Canon VIXIA HF R50 — optical wide
presets.$note: Nominal. Canon's manual (PUB. DIE-0448-000A) prints 2.8 mm at the wide end, 38.5 mm equivalent with Advanced Zoom off, and 1920 x 1080 MP4 at 30P. The sensor is printed only as 1/4.85 inch, so the 16:9 image extent is inferred from the 35 mm equivalent: diagonal hypot(36, 24) x 2.8 / 38.5 = 3.147 mm, which is 2.743 x 1.543 mm and gives 52.2 x 30.8 deg. Advanced Zoom widens the view and stabilisation may crop it; calibrate before reconstructing. See docs/datasheets/README.md.

presets.label: iPhone main camera — 26 mm equiv.
presets.$note: Tuned to the ~69° horizontal field of a 26 mm-equivalent main camera. Varies by model; verify before relying on it.

presets.label: iPhone X — rear wide, 1080p
presets.$note: Nominal. Apple's iOS Device Compatibility Reference (2017-10-30, table 4-4) prints a 60.983 deg horizontal field for the rear wide camera's 1920 x 1080 video. Apple prints no focal length; the 4 mm is from a review. The image extent is fitted to both: 2 x 4 x tan(60.983 deg / 2) = 4.711 mm wide and 9/16 of that high, giving 60.98 x 36.65 deg, about 8 deg narrower than the generic iPhone preset. Apple says cinematic stabilisation narrows the field further. See docs/datasheets/README.md.
